B is incorrect - If proteins had that ability to do that, it would be too easy for accidental extra replication of DNA. We really want to make sure the DNA replication process is as tightly regulated as possible since we only want replication to occur just before cell division. That's why there is only one very distinct replication site in E.coli. However the original oriC site has certain segments of DNA around it that signal and encode proteins that aid in initiating, regulating and continuing replication. Since the oriC site is moved, these proteins will either not be enough or be too abundant, so replication won't happen as normal.

input: Given question: Trc_1: A cell’s genome is contained within its nucleus.Dolly the sheep, was famous for being the first mammal to be successfully cloned from another female sheep during the mid-1990s. She was produced in a lab using the process of NUCLEAR TRANSFER, whereby the nucleus of a donor cell was carefully fused with an unfertilised egg. This cell then grew into an embryo, the embryonic cells of which then differentiated into other cell types (e.g. skin, liver, mammary, muscle, etc.) Statements:A sperm or egg donor cell could have been used to produce DollyDolly essentially had the same genome as the original cell donorSomatic cells (e.g. liver, skin tissue) were unlikely to have been used as they do not contain enough genetic information for healthy embryonic cells capable of further differentiation.The red blood cells of Dolly basically have the same genome as the stomach cells of the original donor sheepWhich statement(s) above are/is CORRECT? Option A: 1, 2 and 3 Option B: 1, 2 and 4 Option C: 1 and 3 Option D: 2 and 4 Option E: Only 3 The correct answer is Option D.
reference: A sperm cell could not have been used as Dolly was a clone of a female sheep (a sperm cell could not have come from a female). Somatic cells can and were used to clone Dolly. A mammary cell was taken from a 6 year old ewe to create the cells that formed an embryo. This was possible as the whole genetic coding for an individual is contained within every cell. No coding is lost from the first cell (egg and sperm fused) through development to adult cells. Thus, somatic cells have all the necessary information to create other types of cells (muscle, skin, etc.) The whole genome of Dolly is identical to its original donor as all DNA information is passed on from cell to cell. It is as if we had just grown part of the original sheep outside of itself (though it is somewhat more complicated). Hence, 2 and 4 are correct in that they are asking whether Dolly had an identical genome to the original. Idea covered:All cells within an individual’s body are equipped with the same DNA or genotype, regardless of cell type or age of cell (after a complete DNA set is made, ie after sperm/egg nuclei fusion)

Thus, the genome of Dolly was essentially the same as the original cell donor. Furthermore, somatic cells are not capable of further differentiation, so the embryonic cells of Dolly were likely to have been healthy and mutation-free. Thus, 2 and 4 are correct. 1 and 3 are incorrect. This is because a sperm cell could not have been used to produce Dolly, as sperm cells are not capable of undergoing nuclear transfer.
